title: Realign — Shoulder Prehab
subtitle: Rotator cuff and scapular stability for overhead sports
coaching_note: This is prevention work for anyone doing repeated overhead motion — racket sports, swimming, throwing. The muscles here are small and easy to skip, but they're what keeps the shoulder joint centered under load. Light weight, high control, every rep.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.form_cue: Small circles first, build to big ones, both directions.
exercises.why: Gets blood into the joint before you load the small stabilizer muscles.

exercises.name: Band Overhead Pass-Through
exercises.form_cue: Wide grip, arms straight, move the band slowly from front of your hips to behind your back.
exercises.why: Opens overhead range of motion before the rotator cuff work loads the joint.

phases.name: Rotator Cuff
phases.coaching_note: These are small muscles — light band tension is correct here, not a heavier one. If you can't feel it working with control, the band is too heavy.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
exercises.form_cue: Anchor the band at waist height. Elbow bent 90 degrees, pinned to your side, rotate the forearm outward only — the elbow doesn't move.
exercises.why: Strengthens the infraspinatus and teres minor — the rotator cuff muscles that decelerate the arm on every overhead swing.

exercises.name: Band Internal Rotation
exercises.form_cue: Same elbow-pinned setup, rotate the forearm inward across your body, slow and controlled on the way back.
exercises.why: Balances the external rotation work — a shoulder that's strong in one rotational direction and weak in the other is an injury pattern waiting to happen.

exercises.name: Band Y-Raise
exercises.form_cue: Slight forward lean, arms form a Y at 45 degrees, thumbs up, raise to shoulder height only.
exercises.why: Targets the lower trapezius — weak here is one of the most common drivers of shoulder impingement in overhead athletes.

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Lying on your side, shoulder and elbow both bent 90 degrees, gently press your forearm toward the floor with the other hand. Stop well before it pinches.
exercises.why: Addresses internal rotation restriction that builds up in overhead athletes and is linked to shoulder impingement.

exercises.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Forearm on the doorframe at shoulder height, lean through the doorway until you feel the stretch.
exercises.why: Tight chest muscles pull the shoulder forward out of alignment — release them to let the cuff work actually hold.

progression_notes: Keep the band light here even as strength improves elsewhere — add reps before adding band tension on rotator cuff work specifically.
